seed: Drag along the ruler and the stretch you dragged over is marked across every track, as Final Cut's Range tool does: a green band on the ruler with a grip at each end, washed down through the tracks, and the In and the Out set together. At Next defaults, no flag set: the recording and a b-roll clip meet at 0:07 on V1; a range drawn from 0:05 to 0:09 across that cut takes a transition from Cmd-T, a cut at both of its ends from the ruler's right click, Delete leaves the gap, Shift-Delete closes it, and a click on the ruler outside it lets it go.

steps.note: the recording trimmed to seven seconds with b-roll butted on at 0:07, the playhead at 0:02, nothing marked

a drag from 0:05 to 0:09 on the ruler, away from the playhead: a green band on the ruler with a grip at each end and a wash down through V1 over the cut at 0:07. The In and the Out are set, the playhead did not move, and the clip that was picked is let go, because the range is what is in hand now
Cmd-T with the range in hand puts the default transition on every cut inside it: the one at 0:07, drawn as a band over both clips

a click on the ruler inside the range moves the playhead and keeps the range. A walk's right click cannot put the pointer over the ruler, so its menu acts at the playhead, the ruler's own fallback: the playhead inside the range is the click on the band
Split at Range Edges from the range's right click: a cut through the recording at 0:05 and through the b-roll at 0:09, the range still in hand
Delete with the range in hand: the four seconds come out of every track and the gap stays, so the b-roll still starts at 0:09 (Premiere's Lift)
Shift-Delete: the same four seconds out and the gap closed, so the b-roll pulls back to 0:05 (Premiere's Extract)
a drag that starts on the Out grip moves the Out alone, from 0:09 to 0:10
a click on the ruler past the range puts the playhead there and lets the range go
